pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK in (high, normal, low). test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' asserts the seeded rows are all normal and that 'urgent' is rejected. I read the tests but could not run them (Bash denied).
item() in src/index.js appends ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. The 'AC-2' test checks the exact <li> text.
src/index.js filters with 'WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id'. The 'AC-3' test checks high, low and normal, including id order.
The unfiltered query is 'ORDER BY id'. The 'AC-4' test checks it.
nav() renders All/High/Normal/Low, with the current one as <strong>. The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.

The handler returns 400 when the priority param is present but not in the PRIORITIES set, before any query runs. The 'AC-6' test covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and asserts no <li> in the body.

The empty message is 'No items yet.' unless the filter is set and the table is non-empty, in which case it is 'No

-priority items.'. The 'AC-7' test covers high, low, normal and the empty table in all four views.

traffic/routes.json is ["/", "/?priority=high"]. The 'AC-8' test asserts the route is listed. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts a query string, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

lenses.note: The spec's decisions are followed: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing is added beyond the spec; the traffic check and fake-app changes were needed for AC-8.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and have tests that would fail if the behaviour broke.

test/priority.test.js asserts rendered output and status codes. The fake app in test/traffic.test.js now records the query string, and the PR discloses this. No tests were deleted. The traffic-config test keeps the fragment and space rejections and adds a query-string pass case. I could not run the suites because Bash was denied.
README describes the ?priority= filter. No other docs go stale.

The input is validated against a fixed set before it is bound into a parameterised query. The empty-message logic is correct. The query-string regex in the traffic check is permissive but still refuses spaces and '#'.
Titles are HTML-escaped, the priority is whitelisted and bound as a parameter, and nothing in the repo tries to steer the review.
The diff touches no CSS or client UI files. The page is server-rendered HTML with no styling, and the PR says no screenshots were taken.
There is no browser flow to demonstrate, and the PR reports no browser session. The HTML output is covered by Workers-runtime tests.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims I checked against the diff are true: the 400 behaviour, the migration, the routes.json entry, the traffic-check change and the fake-app change.
